result:
Understood. I'll write it up. One decision comes first because it shapes the whole design: where the batch tracking lives. There are two sensible options.

**1. Add it to the taproom app (my recommendation).** New batch, sack and bottling tables go in the same SQLite database, with new pages in the same Flask app on the Pi. You keep one machine, one thing to back up and one thing to keep running. The downside is that a bad change to batch tracking could take the tab system down on a Friday night.

**2. A separate small app on the same Pi.** It would have its own database and its own pages and run alongside the taproom app. Each could break or be updated without touching the other. The cost is two things to start, back up and look after.

I dropped buying brewery software. It wouldn't drive your label printer or the scan-on-open flow without a lot of workarounds, so it works against what you described.

I recommend option 1. The two systems don't share data, but they do share the same Pi and the same person maintaining them. Careful testing before changes go live handles most of the risk.

This is a project-sized piece of work, not a quick change, so it gets a full written design in `specs/`. A reviewer will read it before you do, and I may come back once with a few questions only you can answer. After that it's yours to approve. The project folder isn't under git yet, so I'll set that up so the design can be committed, unless you'd rather I didn't.

Which way do you want to go, 1 or 2?
